edits.find:
Before fanning out, find this conversation's transcript in the `agent-transcripts/` directory the system prompt names. Do not glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`. That crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects.

```bash
ls -t <agent-transcripts>/*.jsonl <agent-transcripts>/*/*.jsonl <agent-transcripts>/*/subagents/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -10
```

That covers the legacy flat (`<id>.jsonl`), current nested (`<id>/<id>.jsonl`), and subagent (`<parent>/subagents/<child>.jsonl`) layouts. For each candidate, read the first JSONL line. Take the file whose `message.content[0].text` contains the conversation's opening user prompt. If none matches, pass a tight digest of the session instead.
edits.replace:
Before fanning out, find this conversation's transcript in the workspace's project folder, `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`. The slug is the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-`, so `/Users/you/my_proj` is `-Users-you-my-proj`. Do not glob across `~/.claude/projects/*/`. That crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects.

```bash
ls -t ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*/subagents/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -10
```

That covers sessions (`<session>.jsonl`) and their subagents (`<session>/subagents/<agent>.jsonl`). The newest session file is usually this one, but another session in the same workspace can be newer, so check. Each line is a JSON object with a `type`. A human message is a `type: "user"` line whose `message.content` is a string or a list of `text` blocks. Tool results are `type: "user"` lines too, but their content is `tool_result` blocks, so they are not human messages. Skip `isMeta: true` lines as well, because they carry injected text such as a skill body. For each candidate, find the first human message. Take the file whose first human message contains the conversation's opening user prompt. If none matches, pass a tight digest of the session instead.
edits.why: Claude Code keeps transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, and the system prompt does not name the folder. Its first line is metadata, and tool results share type user with human messages, so the match must find the first human message.

edits.find:
Follow each approved row's Routing exactly:

- Trivial existing-skill edit (a one-line bullet, a tightened sentence, a stale fact corrected): the parent does it directly.
- Substantive existing-skill edit (a new section, a new pattern table, more than ~10 lines): hand to Cursor's built-in `create-skill` skill and run its draft / test / iterate loop.
- `tune description: <skill path>` (the skill exists but didn't trigger when it should have): hand to `create-skill` and run its description-optimization loop.
- `new skill via create-skill: <kebab-name>`: hand creation to `create-skill`. Do not invent the shape ad hoc.
edits.replace:
Follow each approved row's Routing exactly. For a plugin skill, the parent writes its rule file directly, whatever the size of the edit. The rows below cover every other skill. They hand work to the `skill-creator` skill when the session lists it, because it runs the test loop a skill change needs. Without it, the parent makes the edit directly, and a new skill is a `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter under `.claude/skills/<kebab-name>/`, or `~/.claude/skills/<kebab-name>/` for a personal skill.

- Trivial existing-skill edit (a one-line bullet, a tightened sentence, a stale fact corrected): the parent does it directly.
- Substantive existing-skill edit (a new section, a new pattern table, more than ~10 lines): hand to `skill-creator` and run its draft / test / iterate loop.
- `tune description: <skill path>` (the skill exists but didn't trigger when it should have): hand to `skill-creator` and run its description-optimization loop.
- `new skill via skill-creator: <kebab-name>`: hand creation to `skill-creator`. Do not invent the shape ad hoc.
edits.why: Claude Code has no create-skill built-in. skill-creator has the same draft, test, and description loops, and is not always installed. skill-creator's loops test a SKILL.md, not a rule file, so a plugin skill's edit skips them.

edits.find: Never edit a skill under `plugins/cache/`. Before approval, show its destination, `.cursor/skills/<skill>/` or `~/.cursor/skills/<skill>/`. After approval, copy the skill folder there and edit the copy. Never open a PR or push.
edits.replace: Never edit a skill under `plugins/cache/`, and never copy a plugin skill to `.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/` to edit it. The copy only adds its own `/<skill>` command. `/<plugin>:<skill>` and every skill that reads the plugin skill by path still run the plugin's text. Put each approved edit to a plugin skill in a rule file instead, `.claude/rules/<plugin>-<skill>.md` for this project or `~/.claude/rules/<plugin>-<skill>.md` for every project, such as `~/.claude/rules/omc-pstack-fy-reflect.md` for `/omc-pstack-fy:reflect`. Open the rule with its condition, such as "When you run the omc-pstack-fy `reflect` skill,", so it does nothing otherwise. A rule cannot delete the plugin's text, so when an edit changes or removes a step, quote that step in the rule and say the rule replaces it. Write the plugin's version beside each edit, from the `version` in its `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or the version folder in its cache path, or the date when it has neither, because a later release can make the edit stale. Add to the file when it exists. Before approval, show each edit's rule file path. Never open a PR or push.
edits.why: Claude Code loads a plugin skill and a same-named skill in `.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/` side by side, because plugin skills are namespaced as `/plugin-name:skill-name`, so an edited copy never replaces the plugin's text. A rule file without `paths` loads at launch. Subagents load it too, except Explore, Plan, and subagents that set `omitClaudeMd`. So the edit reaches the slash command, skills that read the skill by path, and most delegates. Leaving `project` out of `--setting-sources` skips project rules, and the `managed-only` Project instructions setting skips `.claude/rules/` files. A rule cannot delete plugin text, and Claude may pick either of two instructions that contradict, so a rule that changes or removes a step quotes that step and says the rule replaces it. The file lives outside the plugin cache, so by construction a plugin update leaves it in place. For the same reason a later release can make it stale, so each edit records the plugin version.

edits.find:
pstack is built for Cursor, and it also installs in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins`, then `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`. There, each command takes a `pstack:` prefix, such as `/pstack:poteto-mode`. The [Claude Code adapter](../../docs/harness/claude-code.md) maps the Cursor names, and a step that needs a Cursor-only feature, such as Bugbot or Automations, is skipped with a one-line note.

Other tools can read the skills, because they use the Agent Skills format. But most workflow skills, including `/poteto-mode`, `/how`, `/why`, and `/teach`, spawn Cursor subagents with per-role models, and Custom Modes and `/loop` are Cursor features, so those parts may not work there.
edits.replace:
omc-pstack-fy is a personal Claude Code build of pstack, the Cursor plugin by Lauren Tan. A step that needs a Cursor-only service, such as a webhook routine, is skipped with a one-line note.

Other tools can read the skills, because they use the Agent Skills format. But most workflow skills, including `/poteto-mode`, `/how`, `/why`, and `/teach`, spawn Claude Code subagents with per-role models, and `/loop` is a Claude Code command, so those parts may not work there.
edits.why: The reader runs Claude Code. The skills are native, so the adapter is gone, and install moved to step 1.

edits.find:
Whether `/poteto-mode` stays on depends on how the user starts it:

- Enter on `/poteto-mode` attaches the skill to one message. It fades as the chat moves on.
- Option+Enter on Mac or Alt+Enter on Windows, or Use as Mode from the skill entry, makes it a Custom Mode. It stays in context every turn until the user exits the mode, and it stays out of casual turns.
- Cursor's docs list Custom Modes in the Agents Window and the CLI. Elsewhere, start each new task with `/poteto-mode`.

Link [Cursor's skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) when this comes up. Mid-chat, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` already uses `poteto-agent` for the subagents its playbook steps spawn. To get the same style from a subagent of your own, spawn it with `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`.
edits.replace:
How long `/poteto-mode` stays on:

- Typing `/poteto-mode` loads the skill into the session. It stays in context on every later turn. There is no mode to switch on or off.
- A compaction keeps only the start of a long skill, or drops it, and a new session starts without it. Run `/poteto-mode` again after either one.

Link [Claude Code's skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) when this comes up. Mid-session, "new task" makes the mode match a fresh playbook. `/poteto-mode` already uses `omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent` for the subagents its playbook steps spawn. To get the same style from a subagent of your own, spawn it with `subagent_type: "omc-pstack-fy:poteto-agent"`.
edits.why: Claude Code has no Custom Mode. Its skills docs say an invoked skill stays in the conversation, and compaction re-attaches only the first 5,000 tokens of each skill within a shared budget. Plugin agents take the plugin prefix.

edits.find:
Not in pstack:

- `/deslop`, `control-cli`, and `control-ui` ship in the `cursor-team-kit` plugin.
- `/loop` and `/create-skill` are Cursor built-ins.
edits.replace:
Bundled with omc-pstack-fy, but not part of pstack:

- `/deslop` cleans AI slop out of the branch diff. `/control-ui` and `/control-cli` drive a web or Electron UI, or a CLI or TUI, to prove a change works. They come from another plugin in the same upstream repository, because `/poteto-mode` and its playbooks call them.

Not in pstack:

- `/loop` is a Claude Code command, and `skill-creator` is a separate skill for authoring skills.
edits.why: omc-pstack-fy bundles deslop, control-ui, and control-cli. Claude Code has its own /loop and no create-skill.
